_comment: Drills as vertices of the graph. The key is the drill's id (d1, d2, ...): assigned once, never reused, the way LeetCode numbers are; it is what "after" lists, make prepare and make next use. "title" is what make next, make rep and the commit show; nothing reads it from a file. "file" is the bank file, relative to drills/: the one place an id meets its file. A rep's evidence entry carries the id as "drill" (written by make solved from .drill.json, 2026-10-24); the reps are found by that, never by the title or a filename. "after": [ids] - what this drill builds on; an id is a drill id, a problem number, or a node id, and the drill is not served until each is warm (kg_lib.warm). Filename order means nothing. Seeded 2026-08-31 from the bank's former filename order. "trains" is the list of node ids the drill evidences; it lives here, keyed by the stable id, so a node rename never touches a bank file or a solved copy. "judge" (optional) is the part of the drill's contract that names the solution: the members, steps, conditions or failure mode the rep must show. The judge reads it (kg_extract drill_lead); the reader never does, because the statement's REQUIRED line carries only the complexity bound and the bans (2026-11-05).

d1.title: One From Each
d1.judge: The candidates at depth d are the letters of groups[d] and nothing else. One list holds the letters chosen so far, for the whole run; it is joined into a string only when the last group has been chosen from.

d2.title: No Repeat Siblings
d2.judge: A subset joins the answer the moment it is built, and no subset is ever built twice.

d3.title: Permutations
d3.judge: Every call loops over all of nums from index 0 and decides in O(1) whether an element is already in the ordering being built.

d8.title: Reuse Allowed
d8.judge: A partial sum that already exceeds target is never extended.

d9.title: Record Every Node
d9.judge: Every subset is recorded exactly once, at the moment it is built.

d10.title: Sort Bounded Values
d10.judge: A comparison sort over a value domain of 100 is the fail.

d11.title: Count Smaller Values
d11.judge: Comparing every pair is the fail; len(nums) makes it a TLE.

d12.title: Kth Smallest Bounded Value
d12.judge: Materialising all n values in order to read one of them is the fail.

d13.title: Count Missing Integers
d13.judge: Walking arr and counting gaps one by one is the fail.

d14.title: Next Greater Index
d14.judge: Re-scanning the right side for each index is O(n^2), the fail. A plain list as a stack, or dsa/monotonic_stack.py, is fine.

d15.title: Range Sum Queries
d15.judge: Re-summing the slice per query is the fail; len(queries) makes O(n) per query a TLE.

d16.title: Number Scanner
d16.judge: The head sees one character at a time and builds the amount as it slides. It stops ON the first character that is not a digit, never one past it: every later rung resumes from self.i, so a head that overshoots by one corrupts the whole parse.

d17.title: Tape Reader
d17.judge: Every amount is read by calling self.number(). When the tape ends the cursor rests at len(S).

d18.title: Bundle Refunds
d18.judge: `atom` peeks at one character and consumes exactly one part, a plain amount or a whole bundle, leaving the cursor just past what it consumed, ')' included.

d19.title: Multi-Buy
d19.judge: `term` never touches a digit: every part is fetched by calling self.atom(). `term` claims only '*' and '/': it stops the moment it sees '+', '-' or the end of the string, and leaves that character unread. Consuming it makes the multi-buy swallow the rest of the order.

d20.title: Longest Run of Ones
d20.judge: Two pointers; left advances at most once per element read (an if, never a while). A plain streak counter passes the asserts while skipping the slide, and the slide is the rep: it is the fail.

d21.title: Slide, Never Shrink
d21.judge: left advances at most once per element read and the width never decreases. Shrinking back to a legal window on every step is the fail: it is the shape of Grow and Shrink, and means the drill was not attempted.

d22.title: Fixed Slide
d22.judge: The window's counts are maintained across the slide: one character enters on the right and one leaves on the left, each in O(1). Rebuilding the summary per window is the fail; len(s) makes O(n*k) a TLE. A plain dict, or dsa/sliding_window.py, is fine.

d24.title: Grow and Shrink
d24.judge: Both ends of the window move forward only. The counts are maintained by one add and one remove. Measuring a window that is not legal is the fail: the answers come back too large.

d25.title: Shrink While Valid
d25.judge: Both ends of the window move forward only. The counts are maintained by one add and one remove. A legal window can hold a shorter legal window inside it, so measuring a window the moment it first becomes legal is the fail: the lengths come back too large.

d32.title: Next Day
d32.judge: next_day comes from the engine's date arithmetic on recordDate.

d33.title: Rising Temperature
d33.judge: The previous date comes from the engine's date arithmetic; the previous row by id is the fail.

d36.title: Not Boring Movies
d36.judge: One SELECT with a WHERE and an ORDER BY.

d37.title: Island Key
d37.judge: A window function numbers the rows by id.

d41.title: Classes With At Least Five Students

d42.title: Sales With Product Names
d42.judge: The two tables are joined on product_id.

d46.title: Second Distinct Salary
d46.judge: The query skips past the highest distinct salary.

d57.title: Sales In Each Product's First Year

d61.title: Department Top Three Salaries
d61.judge: The rank is computed per department by a window function and filtered in an outer query or CTE.

d64.title: Last Person To Fit In The Bus

d66.title: Ledger Tally
d66.judge: Each amount is built digit by digit during the walk.

d67.title: Level Groups
d67.judge: A queue (collections.deque). Mixing two depths in one output group is the fail.

d68.title: Count Univalue Subtrees
d68.judge: The count accumulates outside the recursion's returns. Threading it through the return, or re-walking a subtree to test it, is the fail.

d72.title: Find with Path Compression
d72.judge: Every employee on the walk ends one hop from the head.

d74.title: All Substrings
d74.judge: Dropping a repeat is the fail: every count built on this list comes out short.

d75.title: Substrings by End
d75.judge: Dropping a repeat is the fail: every count built on this list comes out short.

d77.title: Each Element Once
d77.judge: A combination whose sum already equals or exceeds target is never extended.

d86.title: Read The Numbers
d86.judge: Each number is built digit by digit during the walk.

d87.title: Read The Signed Numbers
d87.judge: Each number is built digit by digit during the walk.

d88.title: Orders In A Date Window
d88.judge: The one comparison names both ends of the window.

d89.title: Revenue Per Product
d89.judge: The product is formed per row before it is summed.

d92.title: Price At Time Of Sale
d92.judge: The join matches on the product AND on the date falling in the range.

d93.title: Nested Boxes
d93.judge: A stack of running weights, one entry per open box.

d94.title: Longest Common Subsequence
d94.judge: Enumerating the subsequences of a and testing each one against b is exponential: the fail.

d96.title: Largest Of The Last K
d96.judge: Each value enters the queue once and leaves at most once.

d114.title: Sections Under Cap
d114.judge: A section that is still open when the array ends is a section; forgetting it returns one too few.

d115.title: First True
d115.judge: The loop over lo and hi is written by hand and ends on every input; a step that leaves lo and hi unchanged is the fail.

d118.title: Names In Palette
d118.judge: The membership test is on palette itself.

d120.title: Last True
d120.judge: The loop over lo and hi is written by hand and ends on every input; a step that leaves lo and hi unchanged is the fail.

d122.title: One More Cat
d122.judge: The new ratio counts the new cat in both the cats and the animals; a ratio over t alone is the fail.

d123.title: Boys Ratio Order
d123.judge: A heap whose items carry the ratio as their first element, computed by a function; the classes are popped out in order.

d126.title: Held By Both
d126.judge: The one value tested is built from a and b.

d127.title: Held By Either
d127.judge: The one value tested is built from a and b.

d128.title: Smaller Before
d128.judge: Every earlier index is compared against i. The test is strictly smaller: counting an equal value is the fail.

d134.title: Top Down Index Alternating
d134.judge: The parity test is on r: the top row is even.

d136.title: Bottom Up Index Alternating
d136.judge: The parity test is on the row counted from the bottom, not on r: testing r is the fail on an odd n.

d137.title: Subarrays Summing To Target
d137.judge: Negative values make a two-pointer scan wrong.

d139.title: Node Step Pairs
d139.judge: One breadth-first search from node 0. A visited set keyed on the node alone drops (1, 4) from Example 1.

d140.title: First False
d140.judge: The loop over lo and hi is written by hand and ends on every input; a step that leaves lo and hi unchanged is the fail.

d141.title: Last False
d141.judge: The loop over lo and hi is written by hand and ends on every input; a step that leaves lo and hi unchanged is the fail.

d144.title: Floor True
d144.judge: The loop runs while lo <= hi and every step sets lo = mid + 1 or hi = mid - 1; lo = mid or hi = mid is the fail.

d145.title: Pick One Letter
d145.judge: Each ways[i] is built from ways[i - 1]. Recounting every prefix from scratch is the fail.

d146.title: Count AB Subsequences
d146.judge: Pairing every b with every earlier index is the fail.

d147.title: Split The Excess
d147.judge: Each amount sends to both of its targets in the same step.

d148.title: Reach The Far Corner
d148.judge: One breadth-first search from (0, 0). A cell below k is never entered, the first cell included.

d150.title: Top Two Distinct Scores
d150.judge: The dense rank is computed in a WITH clause and filtered in the query that reads from it.

d158.title: Call Tree
d158.judge: A start's parent is the innermost call still running, not the last call started; after an end, the next start belongs one level up.

d159.title: Exclusive From Call Tree
d159.judge: A call three levels deep is subtracted from its parent only, never from its grandparent; an answer right two levels deep and wrong three levels deep is the fail.

d160.title: Positive Total
d160.judge: The parameter and the return value both carry a type annotation.

d162.title: Largest Count
d162.judge: The pass counts into a Map<string, number>, then takes the largest value.

d164.title: Third Smallest
d164.judge: A copy is sorted with a numeric comparator.

d165.title: Reverse Each Word
d165.judge: split, map and join: each word is turned into an array and back, because strings are immutable.

d166.title: Order Total
d166.judge: The parameter is typed with a declared type or interface in which qty is optional; a missing qty is 1 and a qty of 0 is 0.

d167.title: Mixed Sum
d167.judge: The parameter is typed as an array of a union, and each element is narrowed with typeof before use.

d169.title: Fewest Coins
d169.judge: One table entry per amount from 0 to amount, each built from smaller amounts.

d170.title: Plus One Or Double
d170.judge: One breadth-first search over values; every reachable value is expanded once.

d171.title: Fewest Cells Between
d171.judge: One breadth-first search whose queue starts with every 1 cell, returning on the first 2 popped.

d172.title: Node Distance Pairs
d172.judge: One breadth-first search from node 0. A depth-first search gives (2, 2) in Example 1: the fail.

d173.title: Largest By Flag
d173.judge: Two sorts and one pass over flag; a search per position is O(n^2), the fail.

d174.title: Longest Path From Zero
d174.judge: The longest path from each node is computed once and remembered. Recomputing it on every visit walks every path in the graph, and a graph of 200 nodes where each node points to the next two has more paths than the clock allows.

d175.title: After The Drop
d175.judge: Every comparison is against one fixed element.

d176.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Ending At Each Index

d182.title: Bottom Up Cell Alternating
d182.judge: The parity test is on the row counted from the bottom, not on r: testing r is the fail on an odd n.

d187.title: Square
d187.judge: The parameter and the return type are both written in the signature; the body expression ends with no semicolon.

d188.title: Sum To N
d188.judge: A running total declared with let mut and a for loop over the range 1..=n that adds to it; the total is the last expression.

d189.title: String Length
d189.judge: A second let binding of the name s, holding the length, shadows the parameter; the function returns usize.

d190.title: Hours To Seconds
d190.judge: A const item with its type written, in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, at module level; the function multiplies by it.

d191.title: Bigger
d191.judge: The body is one if/else whose two branches are the values a and b, and that if/else is the function's value.

d193.title: Square Of Larger
d193.judge: let larger = if ... else ...; with both branches i32 and a semicolon after the closing brace; the product larger * larger is the function's value.

d195.title: JSON Round Trip
d195.judge: json.dumps with sort_keys for encode and json.loads for decode.

d196.title: Greet Or Refuse
d196.judge: raise ValueError with the exact message; the caller gets the exception, not a return value.

d197.title: Withdraw
d197.judge: class InsufficientFunds(Exception) defined above Solution, with __init__ storing needed and calling super().__init__ with a message; it is raised with the shortfall.

d198.title: Lines Of A File
d198.judge: The file is opened in a with statement and the file object is iterated line by line.

d199.title: Hire
d199.judge: @dataclass on Employee with three annotated fields and no methods written by hand; equality and repr come from the decorator.

d201.title: Words Starting With
d201.judge: A raw-string pattern that anchors on a word boundary \b and takes the rest of the word with [a-z]*.

d202.title: Days Between
d202.judge: datetime.date.fromisoformat on both strings and the .days of their difference.

d249.title: Pastebin Link

d250.title: Pastebin Read

d251.title: Pastebin Expiry
d251.judge: The scan on the expiration timestamp. Checking expiry only when a paste is read is the fail.

d253.title: Twitter Post
d253.judge: The Write API, the user's own timeline in SQL, the Fan Out Service, the User Graph Service, one insert per follower into the Memory Cache, the asynchronous work over a queue. Building the home timeline with a SQL join at read time is the fail.

d254.title: Twitter Home Timeline Store
d254.judge: The Memory Cache, a Redis list, chosen for its write rate; the own timeline in SQL. Putting the home timelines in the relational database is the fail.

d255.title: Twitter Read
d255.judge: The Read API, the Timeline Service, the O(1) read of ids from the Memory Cache, the O(n) multigets of tweet and user info. Fetching each tweet with its own request is the fail.

d256.title: Twitter Fan Out Bottleneck
d256.judge: The highly-followed user. Fanning out every tweet the same way is the fail.

d257.title: Twitter Memory Bounds
d257.judge: Every tweet of every user in the cache is the fail.

d258.title: Crawler Link Stores
d258.judge: links_to_crawl ranked by popularity, crawled_links with page signatures, a key-value store with the ranking in Redis sorted sets. A single list of links is the fail.

d259.title: Crawler Loop
d259.judge: The top ranked link, the signature check against crawled_links, the lower priority on a match, the two queued jobs, the signature, the move from links_to_crawl to crawled_links. Crawling a link before checking its signature is the fail.

d260.title: Crawler Duplicates
d260.judge: The MapReduce that outputs the urls with frequency 1, a content signature compared by Jaccard index or cosine similarity. Detecting duplicates by url alone is the fail.

d261.title: Crawler Recrawl
d261.judge: The timestamp of the last crawl, a default period, sooner for popular or frequently updated sites. One fixed period for every page is the fail.

d262.title: Crawler Scaled
d262.judge: Leaving DNS lookup to the operating system on every crawl is the fail.

d263.title: Mint Triggers
d263.judge: The first link, the manual refresh, the daily run for recently active users. Extracting daily for every user is the fail.

d264.title: Mint Extraction Flow
d264.judge: The Accounts API, the queue because extraction is slow, the Transaction Extraction Service, raw logs in the object store, the Category and Budget Services, the two SQL tables, the notification. Extracting inside the request is the fail.

d265.title: Mint Category
d265.judge: The seller-to-category dictionary of about 12 MB, overrides for the rest. A database lookup per transaction is the fail.

d266.title: Mint Budget
d266.judge: The template by income tier, only the overridden categories stored. A row per user per category is the fail.

d267.title: Mint Writes
d267.judge: The SQL scaling patterns, NoSQL considered, only a month of transactions in the database. One SQL master taking 2,000 writes per second is the fail.

d268.title: Social Graph One Machine
d268.judge: Breadth first search. Dijkstra on unweighted edges is the fail.

d269.title: Social Graph Sharding
d269.judge: Person Servers, the Lookup Service from person id to server. Assuming the graph is in one memory is the fail.

d270.title: Social Graph Search
d270.judge: The Search API, the User Graph Service, the Lookup Service for the current user, BFS with a Lookup Service call per adjacent node. Reading a neighbour's friends without asking which server holds it is the fail.

d271.title: Social Graph Optimisations
d271.judge: A single BFS from the source with no limit is the fail.

d272.title: Query Cache Eviction
d272.judge: LRU, the doubly-linked list with new entries at the head and expiring entries at the tail, the hash table to the list nodes. Evicting by insertion order is the fail.

d273.title: Query Cache Hit
d273.judge: The parse, the cache check, the entry moved to the front, the cached contents returned. Returning the entry without moving it to the front is the fail.

d274.title: Query Cache Miss
d274.judge: The Reverse Index Service, the Document Service, the cache updated with the entry at the front. Having the cache fetch the result itself is the fail.

d275.title: Query Cache Updates
d275.judge: Invalidating entries by hand on every event is the fail.

d276.title: Query Cache Layout
d276.judge: The sharded one chosen. Choosing a copy per machine is the fail.

d277.title: Sales Rank Raw Data
d277.judge: The Sales API logs in an object store. Raw logs in the SQL database are the fail.

d278.title: Sales Rank Computation
d278.judge: The MapReduce to (category, product_id) with the summed quantity, the distributed sort, the sales_rank table with its indexes. Computing the rank with a query per page view is the fail.

d279.title: Sales Rank Read
d279.judge: The Read API reading the sales_rank table. Reading the raw logs on a request is the fail.

d280.title: Sales Rank Reads
d280.judge: The cache for popular content, the read replicas and why they may not be enough. Read replicas alone at 40,000 reads per second is the fail.

d281.title: Sales Rank Writes
d281.judge: The SQL scaling patterns, NoSQL considered. One SQL master taking the writes with no plan is the fail.

d282.title: Scaling Single Box
d282.judge: One box with the web server and MySQL, vertical scaling, the cost and the missing redundancy. Jumping to the final design in one step is the fail.

d283.title: Scaling First Separation
d283.judge: Static content to an object store, MySQL to its own box, independent scaling. Moving the database last is the fail.

d284.title: Scaling Web Tier
d284.judge: The load balancer, several web servers across availability zones, MySQL in master-slave failover. A bigger web server is the fail.

d285.title: Scaling Read Heavy Database
d285.judge: The memory cache for hot content and sessions, stateless web servers, read replicas with reads separated from writes. More write masters is the fail.

d286.title: Scaling Autoscaling
d286.judge: Capacity added and removed with traffic. Presenting autoscaling as free is the fail.

d287.title: Scaling Method
d287.judge: Benchmark, profile, address the bottleneck weighing alternatives, repeat. Guessing the bottleneck is the fail.

d307.title: Minimum Path Cost
d307.judge: Example 1's breadth-first-search error: fewer edges cost more than more edges.

d309.title: Substrings by Length
d309.judge: The outer loop runs over the length from 1 to len(s); the inner loop runs over the start from 0 to len(s) - length.

d312.title: Prefix Letter Sets
d312.judge: The entry at index i is the entry at index i - 1 united with s[i]. Rebuilding each prefix from scratch is quadratic, the fail.

d313.title: Prefix Distinct Counts
d313.judge: Rebuilding each prefix from scratch is quadratic, the fail.

d316.title: Primes Below N
d316.judge: Testing each of 5 * 10^6 integers against its own divisors is the fail.

d317.title: Flips To Monotone Increasing
d317.judge: The choice is made at every 0, not once for the whole string: the smaller of the count of 0 and the count of 1 returns 2 on "001001", the answer is 1.

d320.title: Maximum Subarray Sum With One Deletion
d320.judge: The deleted value reads the kept value of the element before x, not the kept value that includes x.

d322.title: Ring Distance
d322.judge: abs(a - b) alone is wrong: it returns 8 on Example 1.

d323.title: Knapsack
d323.judge: The state is the pair (index of the next item, remaining capacity) and each pair is computed once. An item heavier than the remaining capacity is skipped without a take branch.

d324.title: Absolute Value Sort
d324.judge: One sorted() call whose key is the tuple (abs(x), x): the second member breaks the tie so the negative value comes first.

d325.title: Array Index & Element Equality
d325.judge: The search runs on the sign of arr[mid] - mid, which never decreases along the array; the first index where it is nonnegative is checked for equality.

d326.title: Array of Array Products
d326.judge: One pass left to right stores the product of everything before i, one pass right to left multiplies in the product of everything after i. No per-index inner loop.

d327.title: Array Quadruplet
d327.judge: The list is sorted once; two indices run in nested loops and the last two converge from both ends of the remaining suffix, moving the low one up on a small sum and the high one down on a large sum.

d328.title: Award Budget Cuts
d328.judge: The grants are sorted descending with a 0 appended; the surplus (sum minus newBudget) is reduced by (i + 1) times the drop from grant i to grant i + 1 until it reaches zero or below, and the cap is the next grant plus the overshoot divided by i + 1.

d329.title: Balanced Tree
d329.judge: One recursive pass returns the height of each subtree upward and signals an unbalanced subtree with a sentinel such as -1, so no height is computed twice.

d330.title: Basic Regex Parser
d330.judge: The state is the pair (index in text, index in pattern), cached. A character followed by '*' branches into skipping the pair and consuming one matching character; a lone character or '.' consumes one.

d331.title: Bracket Match
d331.judge: One counter of unmatched '(' so far; a ')' met with the counter at zero is counted as an insertion; the counter left at the end is added to the answer.

d332.title: BST Successor Search
d332.judge: One walk down from the root: on a node with a larger value, record it as the candidate and go left; otherwise go right. The last recorded candidate is the answer.

d333.title: Busiest Time in The Mall
d333.judge: One running count of people. The maximum is compared only after the last reading of a timestamp, and only a strictly larger count replaces it.

d334.title: Decode Variations
d334.judge: Two running counts for the suffixes starting one and two positions ahead, read right to left. A '0' digit gives zero ways; a two-digit value of at most 26 adds the count two ahead.

d335.title: Decrypt Message
d335.judge: Each letter is (encrypted value - running total - 97) % 26 + 97, and the running total adds the decrypted value, starting from 1.

d336.title: Degrees of Friendship
d336.judge: A BFS from userA over the rows of the matrix with a distance per visited user; the walk stops when userB is dequeued, and -1 only when the queue empties.

d337.title: Deletion Distance
d337.judge: State (i, j) over the two prefixes: equal characters advance both, else one deletion plus the better of advancing one side; each pair computed once.

d338.title: Difference Between Two Strings
d338.judge: A cached edit distance over (i, j) first, then a left-to-right walk that keeps a matching letter, removes source[i] when its distance is at most the insertion's, and inserts target[j] otherwise.

d339.title: Drone Flight Planner
d339.judge: The answer is the highest z on the route minus the first z, from one running maximum.

d340.title: Find The Duplicates
d340.judge: One index per list; the smaller head advances, equal heads are recorded and both advance.

d341.title: Flatten a Dictionary
d341.judge: A recursive walk carries the path prefix down; an empty key leaves the prefix unchanged, and a string value is written under the prefix.

d342.title: Getting a Different Number
d342.judge: A boolean table of size n + 1 indexed by value; values above n are ignored. The answer is the first index that is false.

d343.title: Island Count
d343.judge: Each cell holding 1 starts one count and a DFS or BFS over side neighbours sinks the whole island to 0 before the scan goes on.

d344.title: K-Messed Array Sort
d344.judge: A min-heap of the first k + 1 elements; each later element pops the heap minimum into the output before it is pushed; the heap is drained at the end.

d345.title: Largest Smaller BST Key
d345.judge: A single root-to-leaf walk: a key smaller than num is recorded and the walk goes right, otherwise it goes left. No stack, no list.

d346.title: Matrix Spiral Copy
d346.judge: Four shrinking bounds (top, bottom, left, right). After the top row and the right column, the bottom row and the left column each check that the bounds still cross.

d347.title: Merging 2 Packages
d347.judge: One dict from weight to its latest index; at each item the partner weight limit - w is looked up before the item is recorded.

d348.title: Move Zeros To End
d348.judge: A write index that advances only on a non-zero element; the tail from the write index is then filled with zeros.

d349.title: Number Finder
d349.judge: A boundary search for the first index whose value is at least num, then one equality check at that index.

d350.title: Number of Paths
d350.judge: An n by n table of path counts filled row by row, with cells where i < j left at zero; each cell adds the cell above and the cell to the left.

d351.title: Pairs with Specific Difference
d351.judge: A set of the values; for each y in arr order the pair exists when y + k is in the set; k == 0 returns [] before any lookup.

d352.title: Pancake Sort
d352.judge: For each end from the last index down: the index of the largest element in the prefix, one flip to bring it to the front, one flip to send it to end.

d353.title: Root of Number
d353.judge: Bisection on the answer interval, whose upper bound is max(1, x) so that x below 1 works, halving until the interval is narrower than the tolerance.

d354.title: Sales Path
d354.judge: A leaf returns its own cost; an inner node returns its cost plus the minimum of its children's returns. One call per node.

d355.title: Sentence Reverse
d355.judge: The whole list is reversed in place, then each word is reversed in place by a converging swap between its two ends.

d356.title: Sentence Similarity
d356.judge: A union-find over words: each pair unions its two words, and the sentences are similar when every index pair shares a root.

d357.title: Shifted Array Search
d357.judge: At each step one half is sorted; num is placed in or out of that half by comparing with its two ends, and the other half is kept otherwise.

d358.title: Shortest Word Edit Path
d358.judge: A queue of (word, steps) seeded with source; neighbours come from replacing one letter with each lowercase letter and testing membership in the word set, which drops a word when it is first reached.

d359.title: Smallest Substring of All Characters
d359.judge: A Counter of the wanted characters inside the window grows at the right end; while every wanted character is present the window is recorded and shrunk from the left.

d360.title: Sudoku Solver
d360.judge: Nine sets per row, per column and per box, seeded from the given digits (a clash among them returns False at once); the blanks are listed once and filled in order, a digit is added to the three sets and the cell before the recursive call and removed after it fails.

d361.title: Time Planner
d361.judge: Two indices, one per list. The overlap of the current pair is max of starts to min of ends; the index whose slot ends first advances.

d362.title: Toeplitz Matrix
d362.judge: Every cell at row r >= 1 and column c >= 1 is compared with the cell at (r - 1, c - 1); any mismatch is False.

d363.title: Validate IP Address
d363.judge: The string is split on '.' into exactly four parts; each part is all ASCII digits, is '0' or has no leading '0', and converts to at most 255.

d364.title: Word Count Engine
d364.judge: A Counter over lowercased, letters-only tokens, then buckets indexed by count read from the largest count down; the ties keep first-appearance order because the Counter keeps insertion order.

d365.title: Rank One Players
d365.judge: A plain WHERE on the stored rank column: rank = 1.

d366.title: Top Player Per Team
d366.judge: The query of d149 (dense_rank partitioned by team, by points descending) is named in a WITH clause, and the query of d365 (rank = 1) reads from it. A WHERE on the window alias in the same query is the failure.
